craft_notes: Sthāyin: śānta as worship-difference dissolved; bhakti as pratyabhijñā; vyabhicāri wonder at Māyā-standing-as-other. Sanskrit-first: kva bhedaḥ (WHAT difference — question, never answer); aho (ALAS-gasp = camatkāra break before the conclusion); mā smara (do NOT — prohibition closes blunt). Rows: triple-question cascade (what/of-whom/by-whom/who — rows pile questions, never answers), 1 (‘do not’ end-weighted — vain thought cut last), 10 (Māyā left standing as-other — no gloss on the standing). Close: ‘do not’ (the cut). Rupture: ‘Alas’ (questions turn to gasp — wonder breaks the interrogation, then the conclusion). Rejected: answering any question — killed: the verse asks four, answers none; ornament — killed: plainness is the song here, gilding would reintroduce the very difference dissolved; ‘foolish thought’ for vain thought — killed: mithyā is vain/false, moralizing smuggles. Read aloud: WOR-ship, WOR-ship-per, WOR-shipped — WHAT-talk of DIFF-er-ence … TRANS-i-tion in-DEED — of WHOM, by WHOM … THIS-mā-YĀ … stands AS-o-ther, THOUGH-diff-er-ent. A-LAS … VAIN-thought — DO-not.

lines: Worship, worshipper, worshipped — what talk of difference here, in the unsurpassed?
Transition indeed — of whom, by whom made, who walks the entry-course?
This Māyā — no different from consciousness-nonduality — stands as other, though different. Alas.
Everything is pure own-experience-nature. Vain thought — do not.

c1_essence: Worship, worshipper, worshipped — what difference-course in the unsurpassed? Transition: of whom, by whom effected, who enters? Māyā, not different from consciousness-nonduality, stands as other — alas. All is pure own-experience-nature; vain thought, do not.
